chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: The $5 pay cut at the Apollo: grabbing Claude Hopkins before curtain
summary: Hopkins cut everyone's pay without telling them; Autrey lifted him from his seat before the curtain rose and demanded his money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Getting back to Claude Hopkins, you were with him for what, several months, I guess.
Yes, I'd say -- well I had -- it turned out to be so unpleasant thing, and now -- I -- I would like to have forgotten, forget about it, just so --
Why was it unpleasant?

Well, when I worked with Claud's band, it was bad enough. I mean we played theaters, like Howard Theater, and Washington, D. C., and different -- I'm trying to think of where else, Washington, Baltimore -- anyhow, Baltimore, and we did -- I'm trying to think did I do that. Yes, I did do the Apollo with him. Oh, did I do the Apollo!
With Claude?
Ye-e-e-s.
What happened?

Well I mean, as I was -- I get -- I could see the curtain going up, and it got -- we were in the Apollo Palmer Theater, yeah, and we'd just gotten -- it was on payday, and I'd just gotten my pay slip, and I counted my money, and I was $5.00 short. So I started thinking, and I counted the rest, and said maybe I made a mistake. So I walked on and said 'Hey, Claud, I think there's a little mistake here. I'm $5.00 short in my money.' He said, 'no, you're not short.' He say 'that's what it is.' I say well why? I say you didn't talk to me. You

didn't ask -- he said well I don't have to say, because I cut you and everybody $5.00. I said you don't just cut me $5.00, and don't talk -- ask me about it. If I'm -- if it's agreeable, or not, or what -- why? What's happening? (Unintelligible.)

Well that's the way it is, man. What you going to do about it? And all along the curtain's going up. So I reached with the other hand and grabbed him, and lifted him up out of the seat, and get -- and hollered Herman, don't do it! Don't do it! Don't do it! at me. I was getting ready to -- you know.
Give him a punch.
Oh, man! I was going to lower the boom.
(Laughter.)

Said, Don't do it! I said man, give me my money. Don't talk to -- you know, curtain's going up, and I mean -- I don't know. I lost my -- well, I came to my mind, I lost my mind, because had he called me aside and said well Herman, it's necessary for me to ask you to take a cut, five bucks, or something, I may have taken it, and maybe yes, maybe no, but you just don't take my money, and say well that's it.
Yeah.
What are you going to do? What do you want to do? You know. Well I was going to show him what I
anyway going to do, this him!
(Laughter.)
Anyway, so we went on through and played the show, and --
You dropped him before the curtain got all the way up.
